title.value: Countering Language Drift with Seeded Iterated Learning
title.justification: The title is explicitly mentioned multiple times in the paper, such as in the introduction and contributions sections.
title.quote: Countering Language Drift with Seeded Iterated Learning

analysis.description: This paper addresses the issue of language drift in goal-oriented dialogue agents by proposing a method called Seeded Iterated Learning (SIL). SIL is designed to counter language drift, which occurs when agents lose syntactic and semantic language properties due to task-focused training. The approach involves periodically refining a pretrained student agent using data from a newly generated teacher agent, which is finetuned to maximize task completion. SIL is task-agnostic and does not require external syntactic constraints or semantic knowledge, maintaining language properties while enhancing task completion. The paper evaluates SIL in two scenarios: the Lewis Game and a translation game, demonstrating its effectiveness in reducing language drift and enhancing task success compared to baseline methods.
